title: Python file processing with pathlib
when: The user wants a Python script that finds, sorts, renames, copies or summarizes files in folders.
prompt:
Goal: A pathlib based script that processes many files safely, previews changes, and works on any OS.
Steps:
1. Use Path everywhere: root = Path(args.folder).expanduser().resolve(); join with root / "out" / name.
2. Find with root.rglob("*.jpg") or iterdir(); skip hidden names and symlinks; sort and collect the list before changing anything.
3. Read and write text with encoding="utf-8" (errors="replace" for unknown sources).
4. Plan first: build (source, target) pairs and print them; act only with --apply.
5. Never clobber: when target.exists() add a suffix (name (1).jpg); move with shutil.move, copy with shutil.copy2.
6. Catch PermissionError, UnicodeDecodeError and OSError per file, log and continue; return 1 at the end if any failed.
Quality bar:
- Safe to run twice.
- A summary line with counts at the end.
- Names with spaces and accents work.
Pitfalls:
- Mixing os.path strings with Path objects.
- Default platform encoding for text.
- Changing a folder while iterating it with rglob.
Verify:
- [ ] No string path concatenation.
- [ ] Dry run by default.
- [ ] Explicit encoding on reads and writes.
- [ ] Main guard and no bare except.
Output: organize.py with main() and a README usage section.

examples.input: organize my downloads folder into subfolders by file type
examples.output: organize.py mapping extensions to Images, Docs, Archives, printing the plan, moving with --apply
